answers.explanation: The passage says the inconveniences are temporary and will soon yield tangible results, so they will last only for a while.
Unless the money can be spent promptly, Government will doubt the executive ability of the university, so it will not be easy to convince it.
The passage links aesthetics to a beautiful environment, so an eye to aesthetics means consideration for beauty.
The author stresses that the inconveniences are temporary, so saying they will go on indefinitely is not among his reasons.
The passage says magistrates looked upon strenuous work as an additional punishment.
The passage gives training for work, training by work, pride of achievement and satisfaction over crime as purposes; accelerating reform and discharge is not mentioned.
The author argues that labour seen as punishment confirms prisoners in the view that work is an evil, so strenuous work does more harm than good.
The author argues that prison work only rehabilitates when it has a purpose, so work without a purpose is bad.
Demoralizing effects are harmful influences that undermine a person's morals and purpose, closest in meaning to corrupting.
The passage states that the Fund was formed in Malawi in 1953 under the patronage of the Life President.
The passage says the Fund finds sponsors for children's education and runs nutrition rehabilitation centres.
The passage says the Suttons of Australia, sponsors found by the Fund, paid Samuel's school fees and kept helping him through university.
The passage says the centres combat malnutrition by giving children proper food, so combat malnutrition means fight ill health caused by lack of food.
The children are deprived of rights through no fault of theirs, so deprived of means robbed of.
The priest says few beasts behave as badly as man, so man can be worse than a beast.
The passage says the art of changing people has been lost, and that is why the modern world has lost its way.
The passage says most people in the free world treat human nature as raw material that cannot be altered, so they accept it as it is.
The passage says people in responsible positions do not expect faith to change men, so nobody thinks faith can alter human nature.
The passage says materialists of the right and the left both exist and that vanity, fear and greed control men all over the world.
The narrator says Zacharia was just the same when he was cook to a Greek trader in the town.
The narrator calls Zacharia conceited, haughty and insubordinate to others, so humility is not one of his qualities.
The narrator says the girls are drawn by Zacharia's tallness, sharp dressing and leather shoes, which is his appearance.
The narrator says women are like children in their desires and that the girls are easily attracted, so they can be easily led.
The mother cries Money! Money! over the girls' conduct, so she considers the love of money to be the root of all evil.
To take a story with a grain of salt means to treat it with doubt, so the story is questionable.
To cross the Rubicon means to take a step that cannot be undone, so it means to be irrevocably committed.
To pull the wool over someone's eyes means to deceive them, so the salesman tried to dupe the speaker.
To count chickens before they hatch means to assume expectations are realised before they happen, so Ijeoma assumed her expectations had already been realised.
Plans still in the air are not yet settled, so his plans are uncertain.
To be head over heels in love means to be madly in love.
To play second fiddle means to follow the lead given by others.
Old customs die hard means old customs tend to last for a long time.
To lead a dog's life means to live in misery.
A glimmer of hope is a faint sign of hope, which suits a suggestion that gives depressed investors some hope.
A farmer bent on exterminating insects is determined to destroy them, which is why he buys insecticide.
Advice is uncountable so it takes no plural, and relations is the right word for relatives in the sense of family members.
To get on with each other means to have a friendly working relationship, which fits ministers finding it difficult to cooperate in the Cabinet.
Furniture and equipment are uncountable nouns with no plural form, so B is the correct wording.
Adjectives follow the order of opinion, colour and participle, giving exceedingly beautiful white flowing gowns.
A negative question tag after an affirmative statement with the plural subject proprietors is shouldn't they?
The past simple lost is needed after could not believe that to report a completed event in the past.
To stand in for someone means to act as their substitute, and this phrase takes the preposition in.
To enquire into a matter means to investigate it, and this phrase takes the preposition into.
Relations between the two countries may soon be broken, meaning ended, which fits a sharply deteriorating situation.
To be used to running means to be accustomed to running, and the singular subject one takes the singular is form.
To defy a solution means to resist it, which fits a problem that has no immediate solution.
The verb enable takes an object followed by the infinitive to discuss.
Depreciation is the fall in a vehicle's value over time, a cost owners must account for.
In a time clause referring to the future, the simple present is used, so realizes is correct.
It is time followed by a past verb form is used to suggest the action is overdue, so did away is correct.
The light is switched off, so the passive turned off is needed to describe the state of the light.
Lain is the past participle of lie, meaning to be situated, and it is used with the auxiliary has.
Accustomed to is followed by a gerund, so writing is correct.
Do you mind is followed by a gerund, so waiting is correct.
A receptionist is the person who registers guests in a hotel.
One lives on a street and has lived somewhere for a period of time, so on and for fit.
Hotter is the correct comparative form of hot for comparing temperatures.
Used to travel describes a past habit, as in when I was a student.
After I wish, the subjunctive were is used to express a present condition that is not true.
Look forward to is followed by a gerund, so seeing is correct.
Little money means very little is left, which fits saying I cannot offer another loan.
Should have left expresses that you ought to have left earlier, which is the reproach implied.
The correct construction is prefer something to something else.
As if introduces an unreal comparison, as in he were a manager.
Tell is needed for asking the teacher not to be told, and told is the past form for what he told.
The ellipsis completes to he really is not used to staying up late, which explains why he is tired.
Must be expresses a logical deduction from the evidence that he ordered lettuce and tea and is fat.
The conditional implies that she married him before she knew he was a robber.
Being forced to go implies obligation, so Jide must go to Lagos.
Fantasy here means nonsense, an idea with no basis in reality.
Ingenious means clever, which fits a robber's scheme that failed because the police officer was efficient.
Embarrassed is spelt with two r's and two s's, so embarassed is wrong.
Occurrence is spelt with two r's, so occurence is wrong.
Believe follows the rule i before e, so beleive is wrong.
Much is used with the uncountable noun sense in a negative sentence.
Last week requires the simple past returned.
A speech is the normal term for an address a candidate makes to voters.
To investigate an allegation means to inquire formally into it.
To be in the red means to be in debt.
To beat down a price means to reduce it.
To ask after a friend means to inquire about the friend's welfare.
An open secret is known to everybody even though it is not formally acknowledged.
To put something aside means to keep it for some special purpose.
Incidents are unpleasant events, and the plural incidents fits the sentence.
Any longer means no longer, which fits he doesn't play tennis again.
So busy that is the structure expressing result, matching having no time to eat.
The tag must match the past perfect auxiliary had, so hadn't it is correct.
In reported speech the modal can becomes could, so the mechanic said he couldn't mend the car.
The phrase result in is followed by destruction, so the fire resulted in destruction of property.
Should have known is the past form of the future perfect shall have known in reported speech.
The sentence means sudden changes may cause loss of consciousness, which fits the cause and effect described.
Keyed up means stimulated to a state of excitement.
To leave much to be desired means to be very unsatisfactory.
To stand one's ground means to maintain one's position.
To make both ends meet means to live within one's income.
Instantaneous means immediate, happening at once.
Likeness means similarity.
